profile_id.description: PTP profile identifier; 0x001b is IEEE 1722.1 AVB profile

priority1.description: Priority1 value in BMCA; lower = higher priority (0–14); typical for AVB boundary clocks

priority2.description: Priority2 value in BMCA; used to break ties among clocks with same priority1

clock_class.description: Clock class: 248 for AVB boundary clock, 254 for ordinary clock (OC)

offset_from_master.description: Log2 microseconds of offset from master; 0 means synced; adjust only for known calibration

path_delay.description: Mean path delay in microseconds (0 = auto-detect); set explicitly for deterministic behavior

master_acceptable.description: Number of consecutive lost or out-of-sync Announce messages before rejecting master

slave_only.description: Set to true for endpoints (e.g., AVB audio interfaces) that must never act as master

accuracy.description: Clock accuracy class (e.g., 0x21 = ±25 ns); match hardware capability

time_source.description: Time source type (e.g., 0x10 = GPS, 0x80 = atomic); affects grandmaster selection

domain_number.description: PTP domain number; AVB typically uses 0

sdo_id.description: SDO_ID for domain uniqueness (0–65535); used in multi-domain deployments

announce_interval.description: Log2 of Announce interval in seconds (e.g., 0 = 1 s, -1 = 500 ms); AVB usually 0

sync_interval.description: Log2 of Sync interval in seconds (e.g., -2 = 25 ms, -3 = 12.5 ms); AVB typically -2 to -3

delayreq_interval.description: Log2 of Delay_Req interval in seconds (e.g., -2 = 25 ms); match sync interval for AVB

network_transport.description: Transport type: L2 (Ethernet) for AVB; L3 (UDP) is not AVB-compliant

transport_specific.description: Transport-specific header bits (L2=0x0, L3=0x1); must match transport type

hw_timestamping.description: Enable hardware timestamping on this interface; required for AVB

port_number.description: Port number (1-indexed); usually 1 for single-port NICs

delay_mechanism.description: Delay mechanism: E2E (End-to-End, via Delay_Req/Resp) or P2P (Peer-to-Peer, via PDelay_Req/Resp); P2P is preferred for AVB
